To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
limited lookahead policies in the supervisory control of DESs can be implemented on-line in a recursive manner.
the computation of the supremal sublanguage of a language with respect to a larger language is a recursive process and that this process can be performed recursively in real time.
limited lookahead control of discrete event system can be performed in an on-line recursive manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of recursive algorithms for the calculation of on-line limited lookahead policies in discrete event systems.
the development of a recursive algorithm to calculate the limited lookahead supervisory policy for the control of a plant.
the on-line control of a discrete event system using a limited lookahead policy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the on-line computation of limited lookahead policies for discrete event systems is feasible and can be done in a recursive manner.
the on-line computation required for the execution of a limited lookahead control policy is feasible and can be performed in a recursive manner.

, for the class of systems we consider, the on-line computation of the supremal control language can be done in an optimal way, in terms of computational complexity, by using the recursive procedures we present in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the on-line calculation of limited lookahead supervisoral controls can be performed recursively, and hence, the on-line computational complexity of limited lookahead control policies can be reduced substantially.

we show how to calculate the supremal controllability of a given language (represented by a tree generator) with respect to another language (also represented by a tree generator), when these two languages are finite, and when one is a subtree of another, in a recursive manner.
we have provided a complete algorithm to solve the limited lookahead version (for both the basic and the “supervision with tolerance” versions) of the “supremal controllable sublanguages problem.”
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recursive calculation of the supremum can be performed in a way that is very efficient from a computational standpoint.
the computation of limited lookahead policies can be done on-line, and the computational complexity of the algorithm does not depend on the length of the execution of the plant.

, for the limited lookahead supervisory control of a plant, the on-line calculation of the control law can be performed in a recursive manner with a complexity linear in the number of events executed.
